fieldMarks: Adult male: orange frontal shield on the bill, powder-blue head and much black on the back.
Female: brown, much like a female common eider but with a different head shape and a scalloped (not barred) pattern on the sides.
Young male: resembles a young male common eider but with a shorter bill and more square-looking head.
behavior: Forages mainly underwater, often in deep water, diving more than 45 m (150 ft).
Molluscs are a main food at most times, plus crustaceans, echinoderms and insects; insect larvae may dominate in summer.

Spring migration begins very early, with flocks moving north over mostly frozen seas by early April; migrants to the central Canadian Arctic go around Alaska and northeastern Canada rather than overland.
habitat: Nests on high Arctic tundra, both on the coast and around inland freshwater lakes. Winters on the ocean in the far north, including pack-ice edges; less tied to the coast than the common eider and rare on fresh water such as the Great Lakes.
range: Breeds across the Arctic of Alaska and northern Canada; winters mainly in far northern seas, with small numbers south along the Atlantic and Pacific coasts and strays as far as Florida, Louisiana, Kansas and southern California.

lookalikes.name: Common eider
lookalikes.howToTell: Female king eiders have scalloped, not barred, sides and a different head shape; young males have a shorter bill and squarer head.
